maria_sales: Quick heads-up 4e2 NovaMed POC starts Monday. They're asking for a presales plan: reserved GPUs vs on-demand, autoscale knobs, and answers for their security questionnaire. Can SE/Infra/Security pair on a short doc?

sam_se: Traffic sketch from their infra team: steady 600 RPS, average 180 tokens, periodic daytime wave to ~2k RPS for 90s, goal p99 gen <500ms. Workload: multimodal chat + embeddings for retrieval.

devon_infra: For that pattern I'd propose: reserved baseline 6 GPUs (A100 equiv) with autoscale min=1 max=12, scale step=3, aggressive cooldown 20s. Also enable short-burst credits to cover the 2k/90s wave.

maria_sales: Can you give a one-line cost delta I can share now vs pure on-demand? Customer wants a quick justification in the RFP.

noah_fin: Ballpark: reserved 6 GPUs monthly commit ~30% cheaper than on-demand GPU-hours for predictable sustained usage. Burst credits billed separately; add ~5-8% on top depending on burst volume. I'll follow up with exact quote.

aria_security: Security asks: BYOK KMS, VPC peering, SOC2 and pen-test reports, and whether we can support log redaction for clinical PHI. Also they want a compact answer for data deletion policy.

devon_infra: We support BYOK/KMS, VPC peering for Private/Dedicated, SOC2 available. Data deletion: configurable retention windows + manual purge API. For PHI we can enable record stripping and no-persistent-logs mode.

sam_se: POC test plan idea:
- Baseline throughput test: 1 hour at 70% baseline (420 RPS)
- Spike test: three 90s bursts to 2k RPS separated by 10m
- Latency verification: synthetic p99 checks every minute
- KV prewarm: run 25m before first spike

devon_infra: Prewarm command we use in presales:```bash
redwoodctl prewarm --org novamed --prompts-file top25.json --duration 1500 --parallel 8
```
This primes KV and warms GPU kernels without saturating quota.

aria_security: For the questionnaire I'll need short-copy answers for: "KMS: BYOK yes/no", "Private control plane: yes/no", "Retention options (days)", "Pen-test cadence". Devon can you drop one-line strings?

devon_infra: Sure: "KMS: BYOK supported (customer-managed keys)", "Private control plane: available for enterprise tier", "Retention: configurable 7/30/90/365 days", "Pen-test: annual third-party pentest, summary available".

maria_sales: Nice. Add also the fallback plan if autoscale can't keep up.

devon_infra: Fallbacks: route to smaller-quantized variant, degrade beam-size for gen to reduce tokens/sec, and enable queue depth cap with graceful 429 + retry header.

noah_fin: Pricing note: offer a 4-week POC credit that covers up to 200 GPU-hours and baseline burst credits. If they convert to a commit within 30 days, apply credit to first invoice.

sam_se: Ops checklist for POC (short):
- Reserve 6 GPUs in novamed namespace
- Set autoscale policy min=1 max=12 step=3 cooldown=20s
- Provision 200k burst token credits
- Upload top25 prompts file and schedule prewarm 25m prior
- Enable per-route tracing + token-cost export
- Configure VPC peering and KMS BYOK
- Run synthetic p99 checks and surface dashboard to customer

aria_security: Legal wants a short copy: "Redwood does not persist raw prompts by default and can enable no-persistent-logs mode; PHI can be redacted automatically on ingest." Can someone from infra sign off?

devon_infra: Signed off: we can enable no-persistent-logs and redaction pipelines. We'll provide a one-paragraph attestation.

maria_sales: Great. Final ask: can SE produce a 1-page tech summary + a 1-paragraph security attestation and Noah draft the POC credit addendum? I can send to the buyer once we have those.

noah_fin: I'll draft the POC credit + brief pricing delta today and share in the thread.

sam_se: I'll put together the 1-page tech summary (incl. runbook + prewarm command) and post by EOD.

ops-bot: Prewarm job scheduled: id prewarm-novamed-1798882460, status: queued. Will update on start/complete.

maria_sales: Thank you team 44d I'll ping buyer after docs land.
